publication: FAO — Soil Organic Carbon: The Hidden Potential (2017)
text: Increasing soil organic carbon by 0.4% per year (4 per 1000) through cover cropping, compost and reduced tillage rebuilds microbial biomass, improves water retention by 10-20%, and supports above-ground plant diversity. Legume cover crops fix 50-150 kg N/ha/year, reducing synthetic fertilizer need by ~30%.

publication: IPCC AR6 WGIII — Land Restoration and Carbon Sequestration (2022)
text: Agroforestry systems sequester 0.3-0.6 tonnes of carbon per hectare per year while buffering temperature extremes by 2-4C. Landscape restoration combining trees, cover crops and habitat corridors delivers the largest co-benefits for biodiversity and climate adaptation.

publication: UNEP — State of Biodiversity and Pollinator Assessment (2021)
text: Native flower strips 3-5m wide increase pollinator visitation by 40-70% within two seasons. Staggered bloom calendars and no-spray buffers restore bee nesting and butterfly larval habitat, raising fruit set 20-35% in adjacent cropland.

publication: IUCN — Habitat Fragmentation and Restoration Guidelines (2020)
text: Protecting 0.5-2 ha native patches per landscape unit and connecting them with corridors raises native species richness 25-45% within 500m over 3-5 years. Assisted natural regeneration outperforms monoculture planting for biodiversity outcomes.

Regions with high pesticide loads show 30-50% lower pollinator occurrence records. Integrated pest management that halves insecticide use correlates with measurable recovery of wild bee richness within 1-2 years.

publication: NASA Earth Data — SMAP Soil Moisture and MODIS Vegetation Analysis (2022)
text: Satellite soil-moisture records show mulched and cover-cropped fields retain 15-30% more root-zone moisture during dry spells. Farm ponds and wetland buffers raise dry-season greenness (NDVI) in surrounding 200-500m, stabilizing habitat quality.

publication: IPCC AR6 WGII — Climate Impacts on Phenology (2022)
text: Mean growing-season temperatures above 32C shift flowering 5-12 days earlier, creating mismatch with pollinator emergence. Shade trees and diversified planting dates reduce flower abortion and stabilize yields under heat stress.

publication: FAO — Integrated Pest Management and Biodiversity (2019)
text: Mixed cereal-legume intercrops with IPM thresholds cut pesticide applications 20-40% in year one while maintaining yields. Soil organic carbon rises 10-20% over two years under residue retention plus compost at 2-3 t/ha.
